title: Who Can Change Course? An Integrative Review of AI Sovereignty and Collective Learning Capacity
abstract: arXiv:2606.00729v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper examines AI sovereignty as national learning capacity, using France as an application. Human-Centered Learning Mechanics (HCLM), proposed for entropy-regulated representation learning (Tran, 2026), provides a conceptual lens for relating information inputs, absorptive capacity and avoidable institutional losses. Inputs include compute, data, talent, research, capital, deployment and institutional experimentation. Potential losses include coordination failures, administrative duplication, energy constraints, regulatory uncertainty and limited organizational uptake. Regulation also supports learning through evaluation, trusted data access, interoperability and safety standards. The argument is that sovereignty depends on converting distributed resources and knowledge into usable, coordinated and responsibly evaluated capability. The analysis connects this account with neural scaling laws, endogenous growth, creative destruct

translated_title: 谁能改变航向？AI主权与集体学习能力的整合性综述
translated_abstract: 本文将AI主权作为国家学习能力进行考察，并以法国作为应用案例。为熵调控表示学习而提出的人文中心学习机制（HCLM）（Tran, 2026）提供了一个概念视角，用以关联信息输入、吸收能力与可避免的制度性损失。输入要素包括算力、数据、人才、研究、资本、部署和制度实验。潜在损失包括协调失败、行政重复、能源约束、监管不确定性和有限的组织采纳。监管还通过评估、可信数据访问、互操作性和安全标准来支持学习。本文的核心论点是：主权取决于将分散的资源和知识转化为可用、协调且经过负责任评估的能力。该分析将这一论述与神经缩放定律、内生增长和创造性破坏……（原文摘要不完整）
tldr: 本文提出将AI主权理解为一种国家学习能力，以人文中心学习机制（HCLM）为概念框架，结合法国案例，分析国家如何将算力、数据、人才等分散输入转化为协调且经负责任评估的能力，同时避免协调失败、行政重复等制度性损失。
en_tdlr: This paper reframes AI sovereignty as national learning capacity, using the Human-Centered Learning Mechanics (HCLM) framework and a French case study to show how distributed inputs (compute, data, talent, capital) can be converted into coordinated, responsibly evaluated capability while avoiding institutional losses such as coordination failures and administrative duplication.
